body.statement: For every \(p\) satisfying \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), the fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\), the image \(\Theta_I(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\), and there exist \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) with \(V_\pi(q^-)=L(p)\) and \(V_\pi(q^+)=U(p)\). Every reported endpoint is therefore attained by a full trajectory law reproducing the observed cells, the known behavior factors, and all weak-shadow cross-product equations.
body.justification: Attainment upgrades a numerical outer range into sharp policy-value endpoints supported by compatible data-generating laws.
body.gap: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\), establish static cellwise sharp bounds; the present compact fiber is dynamically coupled and generally nonconvex because full-history exclusion is imposed by cross-products.
body.consumer: Clinical OPE analysts can report certified worst- and best-case deployment values without interpreting local-solver output as sharp.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\Omega|\), enumerate \(\Omega=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_m\}\), and identify a complete law with \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_m)\in\mathbb R^m\).  The observable map is the finite linear map
\[
 (O_\#q)(o)=\sum_{i:O(\omega_i)=o}q_i,\qquad o\in\mathcal O,
\]
so \(p\) has \(|\mathcal O|\) coordinates summing to one, while \(q\) has \(m\) coordinates summing to one.  The causal target is not defined to be an observed-law regression: the object bounded here is the full-law functional \(V_\pi(q)\) from \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\), and \(\Theta_I(p)\) is its image over the separately defined compatibility fiber in \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\).

We use finite-dimensional closed-set algebra followed by effective real elimination.  First,
\[
 \Delta(\Omega)=\left\{q\in\mathbb R^m:q_i\geq0\ (1\leq i\leq m),\ \sum_{i=1}^m q_i=1\right\}
\]
is closed and bounded.  Every cylinder marginal \(q_t(h,a,r,m',s')\) and \(q_t^O(g,a)\) is a finite sum of coordinates of \(q\).  Hence the equations \(O_\#q=p\) are linear in \(q\), the equations in \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) are linear in \(q\), and every equation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}shadow}\) is a polynomial equation of degree at most two in \(q\).  There are only finitely many such equations because all alphabets and the horizon are finite.  It follows directly from \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\) that \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a closed semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\).  Thus \(\mathcal K(p)\) is compact, and it is nonempty by \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\).

By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), every denominator in
\[
 \rho_t^\pi(\omega_i)=\prod_{u=1}^t
 \frac{\pi_u(A_u(\omega_i)\mid H_u^F(\omega_i))}
 {\mu_u(A_u(\omega_i)\mid H_u^O(\omega_i))}
\]
is at least \(\epsilon>0\).  Therefore the numbers
\[
 c_i=\sum_{t=1}^H\rho_t^\pi(\omega_i)R_t(\omega_i),\qquad 1\leq i\leq m,
\]
are finite fixed real coefficients.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\),
\[
 V_\pi(q)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i,
\]
so \(V_\pi\) is linear and continuous on \(\mathcal K(p)\).  Its graph over the fiber,
\[
 \Gamma_p=\left\{(q,v)\in\mathbb R^{m+1}:q\in\mathcal K(p),\ v-\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i=0\right\},
\]
is semialgebraic.  The effective projection result \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) applied to the \(q\)-coordinates shows that
\[
 \Theta_I(p)=\{v:\exists q\ ((q,v)\in\Gamma_p)\}
\]
is semialgebraic.  It is also compact because it is the continuous image of the compact set \(\mathcal K(p)\).

Finally, a continuous real function on a nonempty compact set attains both extrema.  Consequently there are \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) such that
\[
 V_\pi(q^-)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=L(p),\qquad
 V_\pi(q^+)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=U(p),
\]
where the last equalities are \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoints}\).  Membership of \(q^-\) and \(q^+\) in \(\mathcal K(p)\) is, by \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\), exactly normalization and nonnegativity together with observed-cell marginalization, the known behavior equations, and every weak-shadow cross-product equation.  Thus these are attained sharp endpoints of the full-law image, not merely outer numerical bounds.
